_doc: Device profiles in CSS points. w/h = full screen (native apps, react-native-web harness, PWAs with viewport-fit=cover). web.h = visible page height inside the default mobile browser (Safari or Chrome UI takes the rest); shoot.mjs uses it in web mode. insets = safe-area insets a full-screen app must respect. chrome = system UI drawn over full-screen shots. crease = fold line for --guides. taps = system areas that swallow touches on the real device. approx names what was not measured on hardware or a simulator ("web.h": the browser height, "insets": safe areas and system bars, "all": the whole profile; several are comma separated): measure before relying on it, never guess new ones. Desktop profiles (platform windows or macos): w/h = screen size, web.h = page height in a maximized Chrome window (Chrome tab strip and toolbar 87pt, measured on macOS; Windows taskbar 48; macOS menu bar outside the notch area, Dock hidden); a bookmarks bar, a visible Dock or zoom make it shorter. aliases map model names to the profile with the same screen (iphone-16 renders as iphone-15). source says where newer profiles come from. Galaxy S26 and S26+ aliases are inferred from the S24/S25 pattern, not measured.
